title: Computer Architecture and Organisation
topics: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access
Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 1 kilobytes is organised in words of 4 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 1024 bytes, and each word takes 4 of them, so there are 256 words.

items.q: A data bus is 128 bits wide. How many bytes can it carry in a single transfer?
items.s: Eight bits make one byte, so 128 bits carry 16 bytes at once.

items.q: A processor is driven by a clock of 5 MHz. What is its clock period in nanoseconds?
items.s: The period is the reciprocal of the rate: 1/5 MHz = 200 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction needs 4 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 8 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?
items.s: Each period lasts 125 ns and there are 4 of them, so the instruction takes 500 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A cache is 16 way set associative and each line is 64 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 16 lines of 64 bytes, that is 1024 bytes.

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 4 kilobytes is organised in words of 4 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 4096 bytes, and each word takes 4 of them, so there are 1024 words.

items.q: An unsigned integer is held in 16 bits. What is the largest value it can represent?
items.s: All 16 bits set give 2^16 - 1 = 65535.

items.q: A floating point format has one sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 23 fraction bits. How many bits long is one word?
items.s: The word holds 1 + 8 + 23 = 32 bits in all.

items.q: A disk surface has 500 tracks and each track holds 256 kilobytes. What is the capacity of the surface in megabytes?
items.s: The surface holds 500 x 256 = 128000 kilobytes, which is 125 megabytes.

items.q: A memory is organised as 128 words of 32 bits each. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 128 x 32 = 4096 bits.

items.q: A memory holds 8192 words of 16 bits each. What is its capacity in kilobytes?
items.s: The store holds 8192 x 16 = 131072 bits, which is 16384 bytes or 16 kilobytes.

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 34616 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?
items.s: The word number is the byte address divided by four, so 34616/4 = 8654 with a byte offset of 0.

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 4 bytes long. The byte address 1000 lies inside which word?
items.s: Dividing 1000 by the word size 4 gives word 250 with a byte offset of 0.

items.q: An instruction set provides 50 distinct operations. What is the smallest number of bits the opcode field can have?
items.s: k bits can name 2^k operations, and the least k with 2^k at least 50 is 6.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A fixed length instruction word of 32 bits reserves 6 bits for the opcode and splits the rest equally between two register fields. How many bits does each register field get?
items.s: The two fields share 32 - 6 = 26 bits, so each one takes 13 bits.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: The register field of an instruction is 5 bits wide. How many registers can the instruction name?
items.s: Each bit doubles the number of names, so 5 bits name 2^5 = 32 registers.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A memory chip holding 1024 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 4096. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 4096 to 4096 + 1024 - 1, so the last one is 5119.

items.q: A store of 2048 words is to be built from chips that each hold 1024 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 1024 of the 2048 words, so 2048/1024 = 2 chips are required.

items.q: A store is split into 8 independent banks that work in turn, and one bank access takes 400 ns. What is the effective time per word when the banks are kept busy?
items.s: The banks overlap their work, so one word appears every 400/8 = 50 ns.

items.q: A control store holds 1024 microinstructions of 16 bits each. How many bytes does the store contain?
items.s: The store holds 1024 x 16 = 16384 bits, which is 2048 bytes.

items.q: An interrupt table starts at address 1024 and every entry takes 4 bytes. What is the address of the entry for vector number 9?
items.s: The entry sits 9 places after the start, so its address is 1024 + 9 x 4 = 1060.

items.q: A cache of 256 kilobytes is divided into lines of 64 bytes. How many lines does it contain?
items.s: The cache holds 262144 bytes and each line takes 64 of them, so there are 4096 lines.

items.q: A directly mapped cache of 16 kilobytes has lines of 32 bytes and the processor issues 24 bit byte addresses. How many bits are needed for the tag?
items.s: The cache has 512 lines so the index needs 9 bits and the offset needs 5, leaving 24 - 9 - 5 = 10 bits for the tag.

items.q: A cache of 16 kilobytes is built as 2 way set associative with lines of 32 bytes. How many bits select the set?
items.s: There are 512 lines and 256 sets, so 8 bits are needed to name one set.

items.q: A cache answers a hit in 5 ns, misses 20 per cent of the time and a miss costs 20 ns. Calculate the average time per access in nanoseconds.
items.s: Average = hit time + miss rate x miss cost = 5 + (20/100) x 20 = 9 ns.

items.q: A program makes 5000 references and 4250 of them are served by the cache. What is the hit ratio in per cent?
items.s: Hit ratio = 4250/5000 x 100 = 85 per cent.

items.q: A program makes 2000 references and the cache misses on 2 per cent of them. How many references miss?
items.s: The misses are 2/100 x 2000 = 40 references.

items.q: A cache is 4 way set associative and each line is 32 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 4 lines of 32 bytes, that is 128 bytes.

items.q: A memory chip holding 256 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 8192. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 8192 to 8192 + 256 - 1, so the last one is 8447.

items.q: A store of 2048 words is to be built from chips that each hold 512 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 512 of the 2048 words, so 2048/512 = 4 chips are required.

items.q: A direct memory access controller moves a block of 8192 bytes while the store sustains 8 million bytes per second. How many microseconds does the transfer take?
items.s: The block takes 8192/8 = 1024 microseconds at that rate.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A device transfers 400000 bytes every second by cycle stealing and each byte takes one store cycle of 100 ns. What percentage of the store time does it take?
items.s: The device takes 400000 x 100 ns = 40 ms each second, which is 4 per cent of the time.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Each interrupt costs 50 clock cycles to service and 1000 interrupts arrive every second on a processor clocked at 10 MHz. What percentage of the processor time goes on servicing them?
items.s: The service work is 50 x 1000 = 50000 cycles out of 10000000 cycles each second, that is 0.5 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor polls a device once every 40 instructions and each poll costs 10 cycles. What percentage of its cycles go on polling?
items.s: One poll in every 40 instructions costs 10 cycles, so the share is 10/40 x 100 = 25 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A program runs 5 million arithmetic instructions at 2 cycles each and 5 million load instructions at 3 cycles each. Calculate its average cycles per instruction.
items.s: Total cycles = 5 x 2 + 5 x 3 = 25 for 10 million instructions, so the average is 25/10 = 2.5.

items.q: A program of 4 million instructions runs at 4 cycles per instruction on a 200 MHz processor. Calculate its execution time in milliseconds.
items.s: Time = instructions x cycles each / rate = 4 x 4 / 200 MHz = 80 ms.

items.q: A processor clocked at 20 MHz executes a program at an average of 1.5 cycles per instruction. Calculate its rating in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: Rating = clock rate / average cycles = 20/1.5 = 13.33 millions of instructions per second.

items.q: A benchmark needs 400 seconds on the old machine and 150 seconds on the new one. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: Speedup = old time / new time = 400/150 = 2.67.

items.q: A program spends 40 per cent of its time in a part that is made 20 times faster. Calculate the overall speedup.
A pipeline of 4 stages runs 500 instructions without any stall. How many clock cycles are needed in all?
items.s: The first instruction fills the pipe in 4 cycles and each later one adds a single cycle, so 4 + 500 - 1 = 503.

items.q: A pipeline of 6 stages runs 400 instructions with no stalls, while the unpipelined form needs 6 cycles per instruction. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: The pipeline takes 405 cycles where the plain form takes 400 x 6, so the speedup is 5.93.

items.q: A pipeline of 6 stages runs 40 instructions without stalls. Calculate its efficiency in per cent.
items.s: Efficiency = 40/(6 + 40 - 1) x 100 = 88.89 per cent.

items.q: A pipeline finishes one instruction every 4 clock periods while the clock runs at 250 MHz. Calculate the throughput in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: One instruction per 4 periods at 250 million periods each second gives 250/4 = 62.5.

items.q: A program runs for 3 seconds on a 10 MHz processor that averages 3 cycles per instruction. How many million instructions does it execute?
items.s: The processor completes 3 x 10 million cycles in the time, and each instruction needs 3 of them, so 30/3 = 10 million instructions run.

items.q: The 16 bit two's complement word 1110010111111000 is read as a signed value. What decimal number does it stand for?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative: 58872 - 2^16 = -6664.

items.q: A signed integer in two's complement notation occupies 10 bits. What is the largest positive value it can hold?
items.s: One bit is kept for the sign, so the top positive value is 2^9 - 1 = 511.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 32 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The lowest value is -2^31, whose magnitude is 2147483648.

items.q: A floating point format keeps its exponent in 4 bits using an excess code. What is the bias that is subtracted when the value is worked out?
items.s: The stored field runs from zero to 15, so a bias of 2^3 - 1 = 7 centres the range.

items.q: A signed field of 16 bits uses an excess code in which the bias equals 2^(15). What bit pattern stands for the value zero?
items.s: Zero is stored as the bias itself, so the pattern is 2^15 = 32768.

items.q: A redundant group is built from 8 drives of 4000 gigabytes each and one whole drive is given to parity. What usable capacity in gigabytes remains?
items.s: The data drives number 8 - 1 = 7, so the usable space is 7 x 4000 = 28000 gigabytes.

items.q: A disk platter turns at 10000 revolutions per minute. Calculate its average rotational delay in milliseconds.
items.s: Half a turn is the average, so the delay is 60000/(2 x 10000) = 3 ms.

items.q: A disk has an average seek of 3 ms and turns at 7200 revolutions per minute. Calculate the average time to reach the start of a wanted sector in milliseconds.
items.s: The average delay is the seek plus half a turn: 3 + 30000/7200 = 7.17 ms.

items.q: 32 kilobytes are read from a disk that transfers 4 megabytes every second. Calculate the transfer time in milliseconds.
items.s: 32 kilobytes is 0.0312 megabytes, which takes 0.0312/4 = 7.81 ms.

items.q: A memory chip holds 256 addressable locations. How many address lines must be connected to it?
items.s: The lines must be able to count every location, so 2^k = 256 gives k = 8 lines.

items.q: A data bus is 8 bits wide. How many bytes can it carry in a single transfer?
items.s: Eight bits make one byte, so 8 bits carry 1 bytes at once.

items.q: A processor is driven by a clock of 20 MHz. What is its clock period in nanoseconds?
items.s: The period is the reciprocal of the rate: 1/20 MHz = 50 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction needs 6 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 1 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?
items.s: Each period lasts 1000 ns and there are 6 of them, so the instruction takes 6000 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A cache is 8 way set associative and each line is 64 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 8 lines of 64 bytes, that is 512 bytes.

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 8 kilobytes is organised in words of 4 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 8192 bytes, and each word takes 4 of them, so there are 2048 words.

items.q: An unsigned integer is held in 24 bits. What is the largest value it can represent?
items.s: All 24 bits set give 2^24 - 1 = 16777215.

items.q: The statement “one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping” describes which of the following?
o: Data hazard
Pipelining
Pipeline stage
Structural hazard
items.s: Pipeline stage is one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Direct mapped placement?
o: a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store
the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
items.s: Direct mapped placement: a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above. The other options describe Stored program idea, Immediate value, Microprogrammed control.

items.q: The statement “the number of bits the processor handles as one item in a single operation” describes which of the following?
o: Word length
Harvard design
Clock rate
Control section
items.s: Word length is the number of bits the processor handles as one item in a single operation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Immediate value?
o: the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act
a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store
an arrangement in which one processing section, one store and one path between them carry out every step of a program
the smallest addressable group of bytes on the surface of a magnetic platter
items.s: Immediate value: a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store. The other options describe Von Neumann design, Disk sector, Control section.

items.q: The statement “a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage” describes which of the following?
o: Random access
Page
Rotational latency
Seek time
items.s: Page is a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition in which a result is too large for the places available”?
o: Normalised form
Floating point notation
Fixed point notation
Overflow
items.s: Overflow is the condition in which a result is too large for the places available.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Control hazard?
o: a clash that arises when the next instruction to run is not yet known because a branch is unresolved
a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine
a representation of a value as a signed fraction multiplied by a power of the base
a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
items.s: Control hazard: a clash that arises when the next instruction to run is not yet known because a branch is unresolved. The other options describe Cluster computing, Direct mapped placement, Floating point notation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Embedded computer.
o: a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself
the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another
the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement
items.s: Embedded computer: a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job. The other options describe Cache coherence, Stored program idea, Programmed transfer.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Micro operation?
o: the leading bit of a signed word, which shows whether the value is negative
one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping
an arrangement in which one processing section, one store and one path between them carry out every step of a program
a simple transfer or arithmetic step carried out inside the processor in one timing period
items.s: Micro operation: a simple transfer or arithmetic step carried out inside the processor in one timing period. The other options describe Pipeline stage, Sign bit, Von Neumann design.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which term is described by “the part of the cycle in which the content of the location named by the program counter is brought into the instruction register”?
o: Status register
Micro operation
Fetch step
Program counter
items.s: Fetch step is the part of the cycle in which the content of the location named by the program counter is brought into the instruction register.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which of the following best describes Page?
o: a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step
a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
items.s: Page: a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage. The other options describe Hardwired control, Control word, Branch prediction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Interrupt vector?
o: the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
items.s: Interrupt vector: the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal. The other options describe Branch prediction, Two’s complement, Embedded computer.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Stored program idea.
o: the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another
the set of parallel conductors that carries locations, values and timing information between the sections of a computer
the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one
a policy in which every change goes to both the faster level and the level below at once
items.s: Stored program idea: the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another. The other options describe System bus, Write through, Speedup.

items.q: Which term is described by “the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement”?
o: Cache coherence
Embedded computer
Cluster computing
Magnetic disk
items.s: Cache coherence is the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement.

items.q: The statement “the copying of the leading bit into the new higher places when a short signed word is widened” describes which of the following?
o: Floating point notation
Sign bit
Sign extension
Overflow
items.s: Sign extension is the copying of the leading bit into the new higher places when a short signed word is widened.

items.q: Program counter may be defined as
o: the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
the storage place that holds the location of the next instruction to be brought in
the number of bits the processor handles as one item in a single operation
items.s: Program counter: the storage place that holds the location of the next instruction to be brought in. The other options describe Status register, Word length, Embedded computer.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hit ratio?
o: an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
the fraction of all requests that are served by the faster level
the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act
items.s: Hit ratio: the fraction of all requests that are served by the faster level. The other options describe Control section, Isolated transfer, Polling.

items.q: Accumulator may be defined as
o: a simple transfer or arithmetic step carried out inside the processor in one timing period
a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter
the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left
the fixed sized group of adjacent words moved between two levels
items.s: Accumulator: the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left. The other options describe Magnetic disk, Micro operation, Cache line.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Indexed addressing may be defined as
o: a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the forming of an item location by adding a constant in the instruction to the content of a named storage place
the input that enables one device to answer on the shared lines
the part that decides which small step word is to be read next
items.s: Indexed addressing: the forming of an item location by adding a constant in the instruction to the content of a named storage place. The other options describe Data hazard, Chip select, Sequencer.

items.q: Isolated transfer may be defined as
o: a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions
the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor
items.s: Isolated transfer: an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions. The other options describe Instruction cycle, Pipelining, Direct mapped placement.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Which term is described by “the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched”?
o: Branch prediction
Structural hazard
Control hazard
Data hazard
items.s: Branch prediction is the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched.

items.q: Which term is described by “a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards”?
o: Seek time
Read only memory
Page
Random access
items.s: Read only memory is a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Two’s complement.
o: a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
the rule by which the processor works out where an item named by an instruction is to be found
a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one
items.s: Two’s complement: a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one. The other options describe Horizontal microinstruction, Addressing mode, Direct memory access.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Seek time?
o: a signal that makes the processor leave its present work and run a service routine
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
the number of bits the processor handles as one item in a single operation
the case in which the instruction word states the location of the item to be used
items.s: Seek time: the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information. The other options describe Word length, Interrupt, Direct addressing.

items.q: The statement “the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed” describes which of the following?
o: Volatility
Read only memory
Seek time
Random access
items.s: Volatility is the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Clock rate?
o: the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
the number of timing pulses the generator produces in one second
the number of instructions finished in a unit of time
items.s: Clock rate: the number of timing pulses the generator produces in one second. The other options describe Polling, Throughput, Stored program idea.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Sign extension?
o: a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store
the average delay while the wanted sector turns round to the read head
one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping
the copying of the leading bit into the new higher places when a short signed word is widened
items.s: Sign extension: the copying of the leading bit into the new higher places when a short signed word is widened. The other options describe Rotational latency, Pipeline stage, Immediate value.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Status register?
o: a clash that arises when two steps need the same hardware in the same period
a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store
a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing
the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry
items.s: Status register: the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry. The other options describe Redundant array of independent disks, Immediate value, Structural hazard.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Hit may be defined as
o: the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry
a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
the number of bits the processor handles as one item in a single operation
items.s: Hit: a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level. The other options describe Word length, Embedded computer, Status register.

items.q: Which term is described by “a way of writing a movement of information between storage places using an arrow”?
o: Control word
Register transfer notation
Sequencer
Vertical microinstruction
items.s: Register transfer notation is a way of writing a movement of information between storage places using an arrow.

items.q: Which term is described by “a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage”?
o: Page
Rotational latency
Seek time
Random access
items.s: Page is a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage.

items.q: The statement “a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above” describes which of the following?
o: Cache line
Memory hierarchy
Hit
Direct mapped placement
items.s: Direct mapped placement is a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above.

items.q: Which term is described by “an arrangement in which devices are given locations in the same space as the store”?
o: Cycle stealing
Polling
Memory mapped transfer
Programmed transfer
items.s: Memory mapped transfer is an arrangement in which devices are given locations in the same space as the store.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Exponent bias may be defined as
o: a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the constant added to a stored power so that it needs no sign bit
the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act
the part of the cycle in which the bit pattern of an instruction is interpreted to find the operation and its values
items.s: Exponent bias: the constant added to a stored power so that it needs no sign bit. The other options describe Data hazard, Decode step, Control section.

items.q: All of the following belong to Basic computer organisation EXCEPT
o: Sign bit
Harvard design
Stored program idea
Von Neumann design
items.s: Every other option belongs to Basic computer organisation. “Sign bit” belongs to Data representation and computer arithmetic, not Basic computer organisation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Polling?
o: the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
items.s: Polling: the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop. The other options describe Magnetic disk, Microprogrammed control, Interrupt vector.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Read only memory.
o: the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one
a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards
the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
the forming of a target location by adding a signed displacement to the current content of the program counter
items.s: Read only memory: a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards. The other options describe Speedup, Instruction cycle, Relative addressing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Decode step?
o: one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping
the forming of a target location by adding a signed displacement to the current content of the program counter
the part of the cycle in which the bit pattern of an instruction is interpreted to find the operation and its values
a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step
items.s: Decode step: the part of the cycle in which the bit pattern of an instruction is interpreted to find the operation and its values. The other options describe Pipeline stage, Relative addressing, Hardwired control.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Instruction cycle.
o: the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
the taking of occasional store cycles by a controller while the processor is held off
a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero
an arrangement in which one processing section, one store and one path between them carry out every step of a program
items.s: Instruction cycle: the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out. The other options describe Normalised form, Cycle stealing, Von Neumann design.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Miss?
o: a request for a group of words that is not present in the faster level
a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
items.s: Miss: a request for a group of words that is not present in the faster level. The other options describe Seek time, Data hazard, Interrupt vector.

items.q: Which term is described by “a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results”?
o: Accumulator
Instruction register
Status register
General purpose register
items.s: General purpose register is a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which of the following best describes Normalised form?
o: an arrangement in which devices are given locations in the same space as the store
a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor
items.s: Normalised form: a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero. The other options describe Memory mapped transfer, Pipelining, Branch prediction.

items.q: The statement “the part of the processor that performs fixed point and logical operations on the values supplied to it” describes which of the following?
o: System bus
Arithmetic logic section
Primary storage
Control section
items.s: Arithmetic logic section is the part of the processor that performs fixed point and logical operations on the values supplied to it.

items.q: The statement “a clash that arises when the next instruction to run is not yet known because a branch is unresolved” describes which of the following?
o: Pipelining
Control hazard
Latency
Speedup
items.s: Control hazard is a clash that arises when the next instruction to run is not yet known because a branch is unresolved.

items.q: Seek time may be defined as
o: the property that any location can be reached in the same time as any other
a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
the part of an instruction word that says which operation is to be carried out
items.s: Seek time: the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information. The other options describe Two’s complement, Random access, Opcode.

items.q: Cluster computing may be defined as
o: the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry
the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon
a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine
a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards
items.s: Cluster computing: a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine. The other options describe Read only memory, Status register, Locality of reference.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Accumulator?
o: a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left
a signal that makes the processor leave its present work and run a service routine
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
items.s: Accumulator: the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left. The other options describe Interrupt, Memory hierarchy, Horizontal microinstruction.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Two’s complement may be defined as
o: a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
the property that any location can be reached in the same time as any other
the principle that instructions and values sit together in one store and are brought out for execution one after another
the taking of occasional store cycles by a controller while the processor is held off
items.s: Two’s complement: a signed notation in which a negative value is the inverse of its magnitude plus one. The other options describe Stored program idea, Cycle stealing, Random access.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Solid state drive?
o: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts
the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
the part of an instruction word that says which operation is to be carried out
items.s: Solid state drive: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts. The other options describe Branch prediction, Control word, Opcode.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Exponent bias.
o: a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act
the constant added to a stored power so that it needs no sign bit
the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
items.s: Exponent bias: the constant added to a stored power so that it needs no sign bit. The other options describe Data hazard, Instruction cycle, Control section.

items.q: General purpose register may be defined as
o: a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself
a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results
the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one
the fixed sized group of adjacent words moved between two levels
items.s: General purpose register: a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results. The other options describe Speedup, Programmed transfer, Cache line.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Direct memory access?
o: the condition in which a result is too large for the places available
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one
a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level
items.s: Direct memory access: a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one. The other options describe Memory hierarchy, Overflow, Hit.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Locality of reference may be defined as
o: the set of parallel conductors that carries locations, values and timing information between the sections of a computer
the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
the condition in which a result is too large for the places available
items.s: Locality of reference: the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon. The other options describe Overflow, Embedded computer, System bus.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Program counter?
o: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts
the storage place that holds the location of the next instruction to be brought in
the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
items.s: Program counter: the storage place that holds the location of the next instruction to be brought in. The other options describe Polling, Speedup, Solid state drive.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Solid state drive?
o: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts
a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed
items.s: Solid state drive: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts. The other options describe Volatility, Microprogrammed control, Horizontal microinstruction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Read only memory?
o: the condition in which a result is too large for the places available
the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards
items.s: Read only memory: a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards. The other options describe Overflow, Interrupt vector, Instruction cycle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Addressing mode?
o: the rule by which the processor works out where an item named by an instruction is to be found
a quantity carried inside the instruction word itself rather than fetched from a store
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
a clash that arises when the next instruction to run is not yet known because a branch is unresolved
items.s: Addressing mode: the rule by which the processor works out where an item named by an instruction is to be found. The other options describe Branch prediction, Immediate value, Control hazard.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Normalised form?
o: a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero
a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
the case in which the instruction word states the location of the item to be used
items.s: Normalised form: a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero. The other options describe Direct addressing, Polling, Redundant array of independent disks.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Branch prediction?
o: an arrangement with separate stores and separate paths for instructions and for the values being worked on
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
the average delay while the wanted sector turns round to the read head
items.s: Branch prediction: the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched. The other options describe Rotational latency, Harvard design, Memory hierarchy.

items.q: Which term is described by “a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing”?
o: Cache coherence
Magnetic disk
Redundant array of independent disks
Embedded computer
items.s: Redundant array of independent disks is a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines System bus?
o: a request for a group of words that is not present in the faster level
the set of parallel conductors that carries locations, values and timing information between the sections of a computer
the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement
the leading bit of a signed word, which shows whether the value is negative
items.s: System bus: the set of parallel conductors that carries locations, values and timing information between the sections of a computer. The other options describe Cache coherence, Miss, Sign bit.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Programmed transfer?
o: a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself
the time from starting one instruction to finishing it
a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out
items.s: Programmed transfer: a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself. The other options describe Latency, Instruction cycle, Direct mapped placement.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: The statement “a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine” describes which of the following?
o: Cluster computing
Magnetic disk
Solid state drive
Redundant array of independent disks
items.s: Cluster computing is a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine.

items.q: The statement “a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level” describes which of the following?
o: Set associative placement
Hit
Miss
Hit ratio
items.s: Hit is a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level.

items.q: Harvard design may be defined as
o: the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor
an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
an arrangement with separate stores and separate paths for instructions and for the values being worked on
items.s: Harvard design: an arrangement with separate stores and separate paths for instructions and for the values being worked on. The other options describe Polling, Isolated transfer, Pipelining.

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 57446 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?
items.s: The word number is the byte address divided by four, so 57446/4 = 14361 with a byte offset of 2.

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 8 bytes long. The byte address 2294 lies inside which word?
items.s: Dividing 2294 by the word size 8 gives word 286 with a byte offset of 6.

items.q: An instruction set provides 12 distinct operations. What is the smallest number of bits the opcode field can have?
items.s: k bits can name 2^k operations, and the least k with 2^k at least 12 is 4.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A memory chip holding 4096 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 4096. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 4096 to 4096 + 4096 - 1, so the last one is 8191.

items.q: An interrupt table starts at address 0 and every entry takes 8 bytes. What is the address of the entry for vector number 13?
items.s: The entry sits 13 places after the start, so its address is 0 + 13 x 8 = 104.

items.q: A cache of 64 kilobytes is divided into lines of 32 bytes. How many lines does it contain?
items.s: The cache holds 65536 bytes and each line takes 32 of them, so there are 2048 lines.

items.q: A program makes 5000 references and 4500 of them are served by the cache. What is the hit ratio in per cent?
items.s: Hit ratio = 4500/5000 x 100 = 90 per cent.

items.q: A program makes 5000 references and the cache misses on 4 per cent of them. How many references miss?
items.s: The misses are 4/100 x 5000 = 200 references.

items.q: A memory chip holding 512 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 2048. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 2048 to 2048 + 512 - 1, so the last one is 2559.

items.q: A processor polls a device once every 25 instructions and each poll costs 5 cycles. What percentage of its cycles go on polling?
items.s: One poll in every 25 instructions costs 5 cycles, so the share is 5/25 x 100 = 20 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor clocked at 50 MHz executes a program at an average of 2.5 cycles per instruction. Calculate its rating in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: Rating = clock rate / average cycles = 50/2.5 = 20 millions of instructions per second.

items.q: A benchmark needs 300 seconds on the old machine and 75 seconds on the new one. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: Speedup = old time / new time = 300/75 = 4.

items.q: A pipeline of 8 stages runs 50 instructions without any stall. How many clock cycles are needed in all?
items.s: The first instruction fills the pipe in 8 cycles and each later one adds a single cycle, so 8 + 50 - 1 = 57.

items.q: A pipeline finishes one instruction every 1 clock periods while the clock runs at 500 MHz. Calculate the throughput in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: One instruction per 1 periods at 500 million periods each second gives 500/1 = 500.

items.q: A signed integer in two's complement notation occupies 16 bits. What is the largest positive value it can hold?
items.s: One bit is kept for the sign, so the top positive value is 2^15 - 1 = 32767.

items.q: A redundant group is built from 4 drives of 4000 gigabytes each and one whole drive is given to parity. What usable capacity in gigabytes remains?
items.s: The data drives number 4 - 1 = 3, so the usable space is 3 x 4000 = 12000 gigabytes.

items.q: A disk platter turns at 5400 revolutions per minute. Calculate its average rotational delay in milliseconds.
items.s: Half a turn is the average, so the delay is 60000/(2 x 5400) = 5.56 ms.

items.q: A memory chip holds 32768 addressable locations. How many address lines must be connected to it?
items.s: The lines must be able to count every location, so 2^k = 32768 gives k = 15 lines.

items.q: A memory holds 2048 words of 8 bits each. What is its capacity in kilobytes?
items.s: The store holds 2048 x 8 = 16384 bits, which is 2048 bytes or 2 kilobytes.

items.q: A processor is driven by a clock of 4 MHz. What is its clock period in nanoseconds?
items.s: The period is the reciprocal of the rate: 1/4 MHz = 250 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction needs 20 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 8 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?
items.s: Each period lasts 125 ns and there are 20 of them, so the instruction takes 2500 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A fixed length instruction word of 32 bits reserves 8 bits for the opcode and splits the rest equally between two register fields. How many bits does each register field get?
items.s: The two fields share 32 - 8 = 24 bits, so each one takes 12 bits.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A store of 1024 words is to be built from chips that each hold 256 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 256 of the 1024 words, so 1024/256 = 4 chips are required.

items.q: A store is split into 8 independent banks that work in turn, and one bank access takes 100 ns. What is the effective time per word when the banks are kept busy?
items.s: The banks overlap their work, so one word appears every 100/8 = 12.5 ns.

items.q: A control store holds 512 microinstructions of 32 bits each. How many bytes does the store contain?
items.s: The store holds 512 x 32 = 16384 bits, which is 2048 bytes.

items.q: A cache of 8 kilobytes is built as 8 way set associative with lines of 64 bytes. How many bits select the set?
items.s: There are 128 lines and 16 sets, so 4 bits are needed to name one set.

items.q: A cache answers a hit in 5 ns, misses 4 per cent of the time and a miss costs 100 ns. Calculate the average time per access in nanoseconds.
items.s: Average = hit time + miss rate x miss cost = 5 + (4/100) x 100 = 9 ns.

items.q: A cache is 8 way set associative and each line is 16 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 8 lines of 16 bytes, that is 128 bytes.

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 16 kilobytes is organised in words of 2 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 16384 bytes, and each word takes 2 of them, so there are 8192 words.

items.q: A store of 4096 words is to be built from chips that each hold 1024 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 1024 of the 4096 words, so 4096/1024 = 4 chips are required.

items.q: A direct memory access controller moves a block of 4096 bytes while the store sustains 16 million bytes per second. How many microseconds does the transfer take?
items.s: The block takes 4096/16 = 256 microseconds at that rate.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A device transfers 250000 bytes every second by cycle stealing and each byte takes one store cycle of 500 ns. What percentage of the store time does it take?
items.s: The device takes 250000 x 500 ns = 125 ms each second, which is 12.5 per cent of the time.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Each interrupt costs 120 clock cycles to service and 5000 interrupts arrive every second on a processor clocked at 10 MHz. What percentage of the processor time goes on servicing them?
items.s: The service work is 120 x 5000 = 600000 cycles out of 10000000 cycles each second, that is 6 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A program runs 1 million arithmetic instructions at 3 cycles each and 4 million load instructions at 4 cycles each. Calculate its average cycles per instruction.
items.s: Total cycles = 1 x 3 + 4 x 4 = 19 for 5 million instructions, so the average is 19/5 = 3.8.

items.q: A program of 4 million instructions runs at 4 cycles per instruction on a 500 MHz processor. Calculate its execution time in milliseconds.
items.s: Time = instructions x cycles each / rate = 4 x 4 / 500 MHz = 32 ms.

items.q: A program spends 80 per cent of its time in a part that is made 5 times faster. Calculate the overall speedup.
A pipeline of 4 stages runs 100 instructions with no stalls, while the unpipelined form needs 4 cycles per instruction. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: The pipeline takes 103 cycles where the plain form takes 100 x 4, so the speedup is 3.88.

items.q: A pipeline of 5 stages runs 40 instructions without stalls. Calculate its efficiency in per cent.
items.s: Efficiency = 40/(5 + 40 - 1) x 100 = 90.91 per cent.

items.q: A program runs for 5 seconds on a 4 MHz processor that averages 3 cycles per instruction. How many million instructions does it execute?
items.s: The processor completes 5 x 4 million cycles in the time, and each instruction needs 3 of them, so 20/3 = 6.67 million instructions run.

items.q: The 12 bit two's complement word 101000011100 is read as a signed value. What decimal number does it stand for?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative: 2588 - 2^12 = -1508.

items.q: An unsigned integer is held in 10 bits. What is the largest value it can represent?
items.s: All 10 bits set give 2^10 - 1 = 1023.

items.q: A floating point format keeps its exponent in 6 bits using an excess code. What is the bias that is subtracted when the value is worked out?
items.s: The stored field runs from zero to 63, so a bias of 2^5 - 1 = 31 centres the range.

items.q: A floating point format has one sign bit, 11 exponent bits and 23 fraction bits. How many bits long is one word?
items.s: The word holds 1 + 11 + 23 = 35 bits in all.

items.q: A disk has an average seek of 10 ms and turns at 5400 revolutions per minute. Calculate the average time to reach the start of a wanted sector in milliseconds.
items.s: The average delay is the seek plus half a turn: 10 + 30000/5400 = 15.56 ms.

items.q: 32 kilobytes are read from a disk that transfers 32 megabytes every second. Calculate the transfer time in milliseconds.
items.s: 32 kilobytes is 0.0312 megabytes, which takes 0.0312/32 = 0.9766 ms.

items.q: A disk surface has 2000 tracks and each track holds 128 kilobytes. What is the capacity of the surface in megabytes?
items.s: The surface holds 2000 x 128 = 256000 kilobytes, which is 250 megabytes.

items.q: A memory is organised as 1024 words of 32 bits each. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 1024 x 32 = 32768 bits.

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 50628 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?
items.s: The word number is the byte address divided by four, so 50628/4 = 12657 with a byte offset of 0.

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 8 bytes long. The byte address 11096 lies inside which word?
items.s: Dividing 11096 by the word size 8 gives word 1387 with a byte offset of 0.

items.q: An instruction set provides 200 distinct operations. What is the smallest number of bits the opcode field can have?
items.s: k bits can name 2^k operations, and the least k with 2^k at least 200 is 8.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: The register field of an instruction is 8 bits wide. How many registers can the instruction name?
items.s: Each bit doubles the number of names, so 8 bits name 2^8 = 256 registers.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A memory chip holding 512 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 16384. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 16384 to 16384 + 512 - 1, so the last one is 16895.

items.q: An interrupt table starts at address 2048 and every entry takes 2 bytes. What is the address of the entry for vector number 22?
items.s: The entry sits 22 places after the start, so its address is 2048 + 22 x 2 = 2092.

items.q: A cache of 16 kilobytes is divided into lines of 64 bytes. How many lines does it contain?
items.s: The cache holds 16384 bytes and each line takes 64 of them, so there are 256 lines.

items.q: A program makes 4000 references and 3920 of them are served by the cache. What is the hit ratio in per cent?
items.s: Hit ratio = 3920/4000 x 100 = 98 per cent.

items.q: A program makes 4000 references and the cache misses on 10 per cent of them. How many references miss?
items.s: The misses are 10/100 x 4000 = 400 references.

items.q: A memory chip holding 1024 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 16384. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 16384 to 16384 + 1024 - 1, so the last one is 17407.

items.q: A processor polls a device once every 20 instructions and each poll costs 4 cycles. What percentage of its cycles go on polling?
items.s: One poll in every 20 instructions costs 4 cycles, so the share is 4/20 x 100 = 20 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor clocked at 20 MHz executes a program at an average of 3 cycles per instruction. Calculate its rating in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: Rating = clock rate / average cycles = 20/3 = 6.67 millions of instructions per second.

items.q: A benchmark needs 240 seconds on the old machine and 75 seconds on the new one. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: Speedup = old time / new time = 240/75 = 3.2.

items.q: In this course, Hardwired control refers to

the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step
a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
items.s: Hardwired control: a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step. The other options describe Control word, Register transfer notation, Horizontal microinstruction.

items.q: The statement “the case in which the instruction word states the location of the item to be used” describes which of the following?
o: Reduced instruction set
Direct addressing
Operand
Indirect addressing
items.s: Direct addressing is the case in which the instruction word states the location of the item to be used.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act”
o: Clock rate
System bus
Arithmetic logic section
Control section
items.s: Control section is the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Miss means.
o: a scheme in which each group from the lower level may go into any of several places above
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
a request for a group of words that is not present in the faster level
items.s: Miss: a request for a group of words that is not present in the faster level. The other options describe Memory hierarchy, Set associative placement, Direct mapped placement.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left”
o: Fetch step
Instruction cycle
General purpose register
Accumulator
items.s: Accumulator is the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Magnetic disk means.
o: a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter
a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine
a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts
the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement
items.s: Magnetic disk: a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter. The other options describe Cache coherence, Cluster computing, Solid state drive.

items.q: In this course, Isolated transfer refers to

a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself
the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
items.s: Isolated transfer: an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions. The other options describe Programmed transfer, Interrupt vector, Polling.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Processor structure and the instruction cycle?
o: Decode step
Instruction cycle
Fetch step
Pipeline stage

items.q: Which term is described by “the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal”?
o: Isolated transfer
Interrupt vector
Programmed transfer
Polling
items.s: Interrupt vector is the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Interrupt means.
o: a movement of items in which the processor waits and carries each one itself
a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one
a signal that makes the processor leave its present work and run a service routine
the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
items.s: Interrupt: a signal that makes the processor leave its present work and run a service routine. The other options describe Programmed transfer, Direct memory access, Interrupt vector.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: The best definition of Direct memory access among these is
o: a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one
the taking of occasional store cycles by a controller while the processor is held off
an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions
the location that holds the starting address of the routine that deals with a particular signal
items.s: Direct memory access: a movement of items between a device and the store in which a separate controller acts without the processor handling each one. The other options describe Isolated transfer, Interrupt vector, Cycle stealing.

items.q: The statement “the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out” describes which of the following?
o: Instruction cycle
Micro operation
Instruction register
General purpose register
items.s: Instruction cycle is the sequence of bringing in an instruction, working out what it means and carrying it out.

items.q: Cluster computing is best described as
o: a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing
a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine
the keeping of the copies of a group of words in several fast stores in agreement
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
items.s: Cluster computing: a set of independent computers joined by a network and used as one machine. The other options describe Cache coherence, Redundant array of independent disks, Embedded computer.
