items.q: A store of 16384 words is to be built from chips that each hold 512 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 512 of the 16384 words, so 16384/512 = 32 chips are required.

items.q: A cache of 32 kilobytes is built as 2 way set associative with lines of 16 bytes. How many bits select the set?
items.s: There are 2048 lines and 1024 sets, so 10 bits are needed to name one set.

items.q: A cache answers a hit in 10 ns, misses 2 per cent of the time and a miss costs 80 ns. Calculate the average time per access in nanoseconds.
items.s: Average = hit time + miss rate x miss cost = 10 + (2/100) x 80 = 11.6 ns.

items.q: A store of 16384 words is to be built from chips that each hold 256 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 256 of the 16384 words, so 16384/256 = 64 chips are required.

items.q: A direct memory access controller moves a block of 1024 bytes while the store sustains 64 million bytes per second. How many microseconds does the transfer take?
items.s: The block takes 1024/64 = 16 microseconds at that rate.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Each interrupt costs 250 clock cycles to service and 10000 interrupts arrive every second on a processor clocked at 10 MHz. What percentage of the processor time goes on servicing them?
items.s: The service work is 250 x 10000 = 2500000 cycles out of 10000000 cycles each second, that is 25 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A program runs 6 million arithmetic instructions at 2 cycles each and 2 million load instructions at 8 cycles each. Calculate its average cycles per instruction.
items.s: Total cycles = 6 x 2 + 2 x 8 = 28 for 8 million instructions, so the average is 28/8 = 3.5.

items.q: A program of 3 million instructions runs at 2.5 cycles per instruction on a 200 MHz processor. Calculate its execution time in milliseconds.
items.s: Time = instructions x cycles each / rate = 3 x 2.5 / 200 MHz = 37.5 ms.

items.q: A program runs for 3 seconds on a 2 MHz processor that averages 4 cycles per instruction. How many million instructions does it execute?
items.s: The processor completes 3 x 2 million cycles in the time, and each instruction needs 4 of them, so 6/4 = 1.5 million instructions run.

items.q: The 8 bit two's complement word 11011000 is read as a signed value. What decimal number does it stand for?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative: 216 - 2^8 = -40.

items.q: A floating point format keeps its exponent in 8 bits using an excess code. What is the bias that is subtracted when the value is worked out?
items.s: The stored field runs from zero to 255, so a bias of 2^7 - 1 = 127 centres the range.

items.q: A disk has an average seek of 12 ms and turns at 7200 revolutions per minute. Calculate the average time to reach the start of a wanted sector in milliseconds.
items.s: The average delay is the seek plus half a turn: 12 + 30000/7200 = 16.17 ms.

items.q: 64 kilobytes are read from a disk that transfers 16 megabytes every second. Calculate the transfer time in milliseconds.
items.s: 64 kilobytes is 0.0625 megabytes, which takes 0.0625/16 = 3.91 ms.

items.q: A memory chip holds 16384 addressable locations. How many address lines must be connected to it?
items.s: The lines must be able to count every location, so 2^k = 16384 gives k = 14 lines.

items.q: A memory is organised as 512 words of 16 bits each. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 512 x 16 = 8192 bits.

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 33981 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?
items.s: The word number is the byte address divided by four, so 33981/4 = 8495 with a byte offset of 1.

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 16 bytes long. The byte address 13861 lies inside which word?
items.s: Dividing 13861 by the word size 16 gives word 866 with a byte offset of 5.

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 2 kilobytes is organised in words of 4 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 2048 bytes, and each word takes 4 of them, so there are 512 words.

items.q: A data bus is 64 bits wide. How many bytes can it carry in a single transfer?
items.s: Eight bits make one byte, so 64 bits carry 8 bytes at once.

items.q: A processor is driven by a clock of 8 MHz. What is its clock period in nanoseconds?
items.s: The period is the reciprocal of the rate: 1/8 MHz = 125 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction needs 4 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 5 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?
items.s: Each period lasts 200 ns and there are 4 of them, so the instruction takes 800 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction set provides 20 distinct operations. What is the smallest number of bits the opcode field can have?
items.s: k bits can name 2^k operations, and the least k with 2^k at least 20 is 5.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: The register field of an instruction is 4 bits wide. How many registers can the instruction name?
items.s: Each bit doubles the number of names, so 4 bits name 2^4 = 16 registers.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A memory chip holding 4096 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 0. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 0 to 0 + 4096 - 1, so the last one is 4095.

items.q: A store is split into 8 independent banks that work in turn, and one bank access takes 250 ns. What is the effective time per word when the banks are kept busy?
items.s: The banks overlap their work, so one word appears every 250/8 = 31.25 ns.

items.q: A control store holds 1024 microinstructions of 32 bits each. How many bytes does the store contain?
items.s: The store holds 1024 x 32 = 32768 bits, which is 4096 bytes.

items.q: An interrupt table starts at address 256 and every entry takes 2 bytes. What is the address of the entry for vector number 9?
items.s: The entry sits 9 places after the start, so its address is 256 + 9 x 2 = 274.

items.q: A cache of 64 kilobytes is divided into lines of 128 bytes. How many lines does it contain?
items.s: The cache holds 65536 bytes and each line takes 128 of them, so there are 512 lines.

items.q: A directly mapped cache of 128 kilobytes has lines of 128 bytes and the processor issues 24 bit byte addresses. How many bits are needed for the tag?
items.s: The cache has 1024 lines so the index needs 10 bits and the offset needs 7, leaving 24 - 10 - 7 = 7 bits for the tag.

items.q: A program makes 2500 references and 2400 of them are served by the cache. What is the hit ratio in per cent?
items.s: Hit ratio = 2400/2500 x 100 = 96 per cent.

items.q: A program makes 1000 references and the cache misses on 2 per cent of them. How many references miss?
items.s: The misses are 2/100 x 1000 = 20 references.

items.q: A cache is 2 way set associative and each line is 128 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 2 lines of 128 bytes, that is 256 bytes.

items.q: A memory chip holding 512 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 0. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 0 to 0 + 512 - 1, so the last one is 511.

items.q: A device transfers 100000 bytes every second by cycle stealing and each byte takes one store cycle of 100 ns. What percentage of the store time does it take?
items.s: The device takes 100000 x 100 ns = 10 ms each second, which is 1 per cent of the time.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor polls a device once every 80 instructions and each poll costs 10 cycles. What percentage of its cycles go on polling?
items.s: One poll in every 80 instructions costs 10 cycles, so the share is 10/80 x 100 = 12.5 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor clocked at 25 MHz executes a program at an average of 2 cycles per instruction. Calculate its rating in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: Rating = clock rate / average cycles = 25/2 = 12.5 millions of instructions per second.

items.q: A benchmark needs 360 seconds on the old machine and 75 seconds on the new one. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: Speedup = old time / new time = 360/75 = 4.8.

items.q: A program spends 90 per cent of its time in a part that is made 4 times faster. Calculate the overall speedup.
A pipeline of 3 stages runs 200 instructions without any stall. How many clock cycles are needed in all?
items.s: The first instruction fills the pipe in 3 cycles and each later one adds a single cycle, so 3 + 200 - 1 = 202.

items.q: A pipeline of 8 stages runs 20 instructions without stalls. Calculate its efficiency in per cent.
items.s: Efficiency = 20/(8 + 20 - 1) x 100 = 74.07 per cent.

items.q: A pipeline finishes one instruction every 2 clock periods while the clock runs at 1000 MHz. Calculate the throughput in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: One instruction per 2 periods at 1000 million periods each second gives 1000/2 = 500.

items.q: An unsigned integer is held in 4 bits. What is the largest value it can represent?
items.s: All 4 bits set give 2^4 - 1 = 15.

items.q: A signed integer in two's complement notation occupies 24 bits. What is the largest positive value it can hold?
items.s: One bit is kept for the sign, so the top positive value is 2^23 - 1 = 8388607.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 10 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The lowest value is -2^9, whose magnitude is 512.

items.q: A signed field of 12 bits uses an excess code in which the bias equals 2^(11). What bit pattern stands for the value zero?
items.s: Zero is stored as the bias itself, so the pattern is 2^11 = 2048.

items.q: A redundant group is built from 3 drives of 1000 gigabytes each and one whole drive is given to parity. What usable capacity in gigabytes remains?
items.s: The data drives number 3 - 1 = 2, so the usable space is 2 x 1000 = 2000 gigabytes.

items.q: A disk surface has 500 tracks and each track holds 128 kilobytes. What is the capacity of the surface in megabytes?
items.s: The surface holds 500 x 128 = 64000 kilobytes, which is 62 megabytes.

items.q: A memory holds 4096 words of 32 bits each. What is its capacity in kilobytes?
items.s: The store holds 4096 x 32 = 131072 bits, which is 16384 bytes or 16 kilobytes.

items.q: A fixed length instruction word of 16 bits reserves 8 bits for the opcode and splits the rest equally between two register fields. How many bits does each register field get?
items.s: The two fields share 16 - 8 = 8 bits, so each one takes 4 bits.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A cache of 8 kilobytes is built as 8 way set associative with lines of 32 bytes. How many bits select the set?
items.s: There are 256 lines and 32 sets, so 5 bits are needed to name one set.

items.q: A cache answers a hit in 1 ns, misses 25 per cent of the time and a miss costs 100 ns. Calculate the average time per access in nanoseconds.
items.s: Average = hit time + miss rate x miss cost = 1 + (25/100) x 100 = 26 ns.

items.q: A cache is 16 way set associative and each line is 16 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 16 lines of 16 bytes, that is 256 bytes.

items.q: A store of 8192 words is to be built from chips that each hold 128 words. How many chips are needed?
items.s: Each chip supplies 128 of the 8192 words, so 8192/128 = 64 chips are required.

items.q: A direct memory access controller moves a block of 4096 bytes while the store sustains 32 million bytes per second. How many microseconds does the transfer take?
items.s: The block takes 4096/32 = 128 microseconds at that rate.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Each interrupt costs 100 clock cycles to service and 2000 interrupts arrive every second on a processor clocked at 2 MHz. What percentage of the processor time goes on servicing them?
items.s: The service work is 100 x 2000 = 200000 cycles out of 2000000 cycles each second, that is 10 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A program runs 4 million arithmetic instructions at 2 cycles each and 3 million load instructions at 5 cycles each. Calculate its average cycles per instruction.
items.s: Total cycles = 4 x 2 + 3 x 5 = 23 for 7 million instructions, so the average is 23/7 = 3.29.

items.q: A program of 1 million instructions runs at 2 cycles per instruction on a 500 MHz processor. Calculate its execution time in milliseconds.
items.s: Time = instructions x cycles each / rate = 1 x 2 / 500 MHz = 4 ms.

items.q: A program runs for 10 seconds on a 2 MHz processor that averages 3 cycles per instruction. How many million instructions does it execute?
items.s: The processor completes 10 x 2 million cycles in the time, and each instruction needs 3 of them, so 20/3 = 6.67 million instructions run.

items.q: The 8 bit two's complement word 10000001 is read as a signed value. What decimal number does it stand for?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative: 129 - 2^8 = -127.

items.q: A floating point format keeps its exponent in 11 bits using an excess code. What is the bias that is subtracted when the value is worked out?
items.s: The stored field runs from zero to 2047, so a bias of 2^10 - 1 = 1023 centres the range.

items.q: A control store holds 512 microinstructions of 16 bits each. How many bytes does the store contain?
items.s: The store holds 512 x 16 = 8192 bits, which is 1024 bytes.

items.q: A directly mapped cache of 4 kilobytes has lines of 16 bytes and the processor issues 20 bit byte addresses. How many bits are needed for the tag?
items.s: The cache has 256 lines so the index needs 8 bits and the offset needs 4, leaving 20 - 8 - 4 = 8 bits for the tag.

items.q: A device transfers 500000 bytes every second by cycle stealing and each byte takes one store cycle of 200 ns. What percentage of the store time does it take?
items.s: The device takes 500000 x 200 ns = 100 ms each second, which is 10 per cent of the time.

items.q: A program spends 20 per cent of its time in a part that is made 5 times faster. Calculate the overall speedup.
A pipeline of 8 stages runs 20 instructions with no stalls, while the unpipelined form needs 8 cycles per instruction. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: The pipeline takes 27 cycles where the plain form takes 20 x 8, so the speedup is 5.93.

items.q: A pipeline of 5 stages runs 200 instructions without stalls. Calculate its efficiency in per cent.
items.s: Efficiency = 200/(5 + 200 - 1) x 100 = 98.04 per cent.

items.q: A signed field of 8 bits uses an excess code in which the bias equals 2^(7). What bit pattern stands for the value zero?
items.s: Zero is stored as the bias itself, so the pattern is 2^7 = 128.

items.q: A memory chip holds 512 addressable locations. How many address lines must be connected to it?
items.s: The lines must be able to count every location, so 2^k = 512 gives k = 9 lines.

items.q: A memory is organised as 1024 words of 16 bits each. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 1024 x 16 = 16384 bits.

items.q: A memory holds 8192 words of 32 bits each. What is its capacity in kilobytes?
items.s: The store holds 8192 x 32 = 262144 bits, which is 32768 bytes or 32 kilobytes.

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 55522 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?
items.s: The word number is the byte address divided by four, so 55522/4 = 13880 with a byte offset of 2.

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 16 bytes long. The byte address 18750 lies inside which word?
items.s: Dividing 18750 by the word size 16 gives word 1171 with a byte offset of 14.

items.q: A data bus is 32 bits wide. How many bytes can it carry in a single transfer?
items.s: Eight bits make one byte, so 32 bits carry 4 bytes at once.

items.q: An instruction needs 10 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 5 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?
items.s: Each period lasts 200 ns and there are 10 of them, so the instruction takes 2000 ns.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: An instruction set provides 9 distinct operations. What is the smallest number of bits the opcode field can have?
items.s: k bits can name 2^k operations, and the least k with 2^k at least 9 is 4.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: A memory chip holding 2048 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 16384. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 16384 to 16384 + 2048 - 1, so the last one is 18431.

items.q: An interrupt table starts at address 2048 and every entry takes 2 bytes. What is the address of the entry for vector number 40?
items.s: The entry sits 40 places after the start, so its address is 2048 + 40 x 2 = 2128.

items.q: A cache of 128 kilobytes is divided into lines of 8 bytes. How many lines does it contain?
items.s: The cache holds 131072 bytes and each line takes 8 of them, so there are 16384 lines.

items.q: A cache of 128 kilobytes is built as 4 way set associative with lines of 64 bytes. How many bits select the set?
items.s: There are 2048 lines and 512 sets, so 9 bits are needed to name one set.

items.q: A cache answers a hit in 10 ns, misses 25 per cent of the time and a miss costs 80 ns. Calculate the average time per access in nanoseconds.
items.s: Average = hit time + miss rate x miss cost = 10 + (25/100) x 80 = 30 ns.

items.q: A program makes 2500 references and 2375 of them are served by the cache. What is the hit ratio in per cent?
items.s: Hit ratio = 2375/2500 x 100 = 95 per cent.

items.q: A program makes 8000 references and the cache misses on 8 per cent of them. How many references miss?
items.s: The misses are 8/100 x 8000 = 640 references.

items.q: A cache is 4 way set associative and each line is 128 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 4 lines of 128 bytes, that is 512 bytes.

items.q: A cache is 2 way set associative and each line is 32 bytes. How many bytes are held in one set?
items.s: One set holds 2 lines of 32 bytes, that is 64 bytes.

items.q: A memory chip holding 2048 locations is mapped so that its first location is at address 32768. What is the address of its last location?
items.s: The addresses run from 32768 to 32768 + 2048 - 1, so the last one is 34815.

items.q: A store with a total capacity of 4 kilobytes is organised in words of 2 bytes. How many words does it hold?
items.s: The store holds 4096 bytes, and each word takes 2 of them, so there are 2048 words.

items.q: A direct memory access controller moves a block of 8192 bytes while the store sustains 4 million bytes per second. How many microseconds does the transfer take?
items.s: The block takes 8192/4 = 2048 microseconds at that rate.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Each interrupt costs 120 clock cycles to service and 1000 interrupts arrive every second on a processor clocked at 1 MHz. What percentage of the processor time goes on servicing them?
items.s: The service work is 120 x 1000 = 120000 cycles out of 1000000 cycles each second, that is 12 per cent.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A processor polls a device once every 40 instructions and each poll costs 20 cycles. What percentage of its cycles go on polling?

items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: A program runs 2 million arithmetic instructions at 4 cycles each and 5 million load instructions at 4 cycles each. Calculate its average cycles per instruction.
items.s: Total cycles = 2 x 4 + 5 x 4 = 28 for 7 million instructions, so the average is 28/7 = 4.

items.q: A program of 3 million instructions runs at 2 cycles per instruction on a 200 MHz processor. Calculate its execution time in milliseconds.
items.s: Time = instructions x cycles each / rate = 3 x 2 / 200 MHz = 30 ms.

items.q: A processor clocked at 200 MHz executes a program at an average of 4 cycles per instruction. Calculate its rating in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: Rating = clock rate / average cycles = 200/4 = 50 millions of instructions per second.

items.q: A benchmark needs 240 seconds on the old machine and 120 seconds on the new one. Calculate the speedup.
items.s: Speedup = old time / new time = 240/120 = 2.

items.q: A pipeline of 6 stages runs 100 instructions without any stall. How many clock cycles are needed in all?
items.s: The first instruction fills the pipe in 6 cycles and each later one adds a single cycle, so 6 + 100 - 1 = 105.

items.q: A pipeline finishes one instruction every 3 clock periods while the clock runs at 500 MHz. Calculate the throughput in millions of instructions per second.
items.s: One instruction per 3 periods at 500 million periods each second gives 500/3 = 166.7.

items.q: A program runs for 3 seconds on a 1 MHz processor that averages 4 cycles per instruction. How many million instructions does it execute?
items.s: The processor completes 3 x 1 million cycles in the time, and each instruction needs 4 of them, so 3/4 = 0.75 million instructions run.

items.q: The 12 bit two's complement word 100011100000 is read as a signed value. What decimal number does it stand for?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative: 2272 - 2^12 = -1824.

items.q: An unsigned integer is held in 8 bits. What is the largest value it can represent?
items.s: All 8 bits set give 2^8 - 1 = 255.

items.q: A signed integer in two's complement notation occupies 8 bits. What is the largest positive value it can hold?
items.s: One bit is kept for the sign, so the top positive value is 2^7 - 1 = 127.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 16 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The lowest value is -2^15, whose magnitude is 32768.

items.q: A floating point format has one sign bit, 5 exponent bits and 52 fraction bits. How many bits long is one word?
items.s: The word holds 1 + 5 + 52 = 58 bits in all.

items.q: A redundant group is built from 5 drives of 250 gigabytes each and one whole drive is given to parity. What usable capacity in gigabytes remains?
items.s: The data drives number 5 - 1 = 4, so the usable space is 4 x 250 = 1000 gigabytes.

items.q: A disk has an average seek of 5 ms and turns at 10000 revolutions per minute. Calculate the average time to reach the start of a wanted sector in milliseconds.
items.s: The average delay is the seek plus half a turn: 5 + 30000/10000 = 8 ms.

items.q: 128 kilobytes are read from a disk that transfers 16 megabytes every second. Calculate the transfer time in milliseconds.
items.s: 128 kilobytes is 0.125 megabytes, which takes 0.125/16 = 7.81 ms.

items.q: A store is split into 2 independent banks that work in turn, and one bank access takes 250 ns. What is the effective time per word when the banks are kept busy?
items.s: The banks overlap their work, so one word appears every 250/2 = 125 ns.

items.q: A control store holds 1024 microinstructions of 48 bits each. How many bytes does the store contain?
items.s: The store holds 1024 x 48 = 49152 bits, which is 6144 bytes.

items.q: A directly mapped cache of 32 kilobytes has lines of 64 bytes and the processor issues 32 bit byte addresses. How many bits are needed for the tag?
items.s: The cache has 512 lines so the index needs 9 bits and the offset needs 6, leaving 32 - 9 - 6 = 17 bits for the tag.

items.q: A device transfers 250000 bytes every second by cycle stealing and each byte takes one store cycle of 100 ns. What percentage of the store time does it take?
items.s: The device takes 250000 x 100 ns = 25 ms each second, which is 2.5 per cent of the time.

items.q: A pipeline of 4 stages runs 20 instructions without stalls. Calculate its efficiency in per cent.

items.q: A memory holds 8192 words of 8 bits each. What is its capacity in kilobytes?

items.q: A byte addressable store uses words of four bytes. The byte address 8084 is presented to it. Which word number does that byte belong to?

items.q: In a byte addressable store each word is 2 bytes long. The byte address 958 lies inside which word?

items.q: An instruction needs 16 clock periods to complete on a processor clocked at 4 MHz. How many nanoseconds does it take?

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above”
o: Direct mapped placement
Write through
Cache line
Miss
items.s: Direct mapped placement is a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage”
o: Seek time
Read only memory
Chip select
Page
items.s: Page is a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage.

items.q: Hardwired control may be defined as
o: a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step
the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
a way of writing a movement of information between storage places using an arrow
items.s: Hardwired control: a fixed network of gates that produces the timing signals for every step. The other options describe Register transfer notation, Microprogrammed control, Control word.

items.q: In this course, Accumulator refers to
o: the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left
the holding place for the bit pattern that is currently being interpreted
a simple transfer or arithmetic step carried out inside the processor in one timing period
the part of the cycle in which the content of the location named by the program counter is brought into the instruction register
items.s: Accumulator: the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left. The other options describe Instruction register, Micro operation, Fetch step.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Microprogrammed control.
o: the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
a way of writing a movement of information between storage places using an arrow
items.s: Microprogrammed control: a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store. The other options describe Horizontal microinstruction, Register transfer notation, Control word.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing”
o: Redundant array of independent disks
Cluster computing
Solid state drive
Embedded computer
items.s: Redundant array of independent disks is a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Hit?
o: a policy in which every change goes to both the faster level and the level below at once
a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
a scheme in which each group from the lower level may go into any of several places above
a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level
items.s: Hit: a request for a group of words that is already present in the faster level. The other options describe Direct mapped placement, Write through, Set associative placement.

items.q: In this course, Polling refers to
o: the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop
an arrangement in which devices have their own space and are reached by special instructions
a signal that makes the processor leave its present work and run a service routine
the taking of occasional store cycles by a controller while the processor is held off
items.s: Polling: the repeated testing of a device status by the processor in a loop. The other options describe Isolated transfer, Interrupt, Cycle stealing.
items.t: Input output, interrupts and direct memory access

items.q: Solid state drive may be defined as
o: a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter
a group of drives used together with extra copies or parity so that one failure loses nothing
a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts
a small processor built into a device to carry out one dedicated job
items.s: Solid state drive: a store built from semiconductor cells with no moving parts. The other options describe Redundant array of independent disks, Magnetic disk, Embedded computer.

items.q: “a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results” is the definition of
o: Micro operation
General purpose register
Instruction cycle
Instruction register
items.s: General purpose register is a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pipelining?
o: a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the guessing of the outcome of a jump in advance so that useful work can be fetched
the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor
the time from starting one instruction to finishing it
items.s: Pipelining: the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor. The other options describe Branch prediction, Data hazard, Latency.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Set associative placement.
o: a policy in which every change goes to both the faster level and the level below at once
a scheme in which each group from the lower level may go into any of several places above
a scheme in which each group from the lower level can go into exactly one place above
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
items.s: Set associative placement: a scheme in which each group from the lower level may go into any of several places above. The other options describe Direct mapped placement, Write through, Memory hierarchy.

items.q: “a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter” is the definition of
o: Magnetic disk
Redundant array of independent disks
Solid state drive
Embedded computer
items.s: Magnetic disk is a direct access store in which information sits on concentric tracks of a spinning platter.

items.q: Control section may be defined as
o: the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act
the set of parallel conductors that carries locations, values and timing information between the sections of a computer
an arrangement in which one processing section, one store and one path between them carry out every step of a program
the number of timing pulses the generator produces in one second
items.s: Control section: the part of the processor that interprets each instruction and sends the signals that make the other parts act. The other options describe Clock rate, Von Neumann design, System bus.

items.q: In this course, Instruction register refers to
o: the holding place for the bit pattern that is currently being interpreted
a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results
the part of the cycle in which the content of the location named by the program counter is brought into the instruction register
the working storage inside the processor where one value of an operation is placed and the result is left
items.s: Instruction register: the holding place for the bit pattern that is currently being interpreted. The other options describe Accumulator, General purpose register, Fetch step.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: In this course, Seek time refers to
o: the input that enables one device to answer on the shared lines
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards
the average delay while the wanted sector turns round to the read head
items.s: Seek time: the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information. The other options describe Read only memory, Rotational latency, Chip select.

items.q: The correct meaning of General purpose register is
o: the part of the cycle in which the content of the location named by the program counter is brought into the instruction register
the storage place that holds the location of the next instruction to be brought in
a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results
a simple transfer or arithmetic step carried out inside the processor in one timing period
items.s: General purpose register: a named storage location inside the processor that the programmer may use freely for values and results. The other options describe Micro operation, Fetch step, Program counter.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: In this course, Microprogrammed control refers to
o: a wide format in which one bit directly enables one individual action
a narrow format in which actions are selected by coded fields that a decoder expands
a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store
the bit pattern that selects which transfers happen in one step
items.s: Microprogrammed control: a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store. The other options describe Horizontal microinstruction, Control word, Vertical microinstruction.

items.q: The correct meaning of Disk sector is
o: the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed
the smallest addressable group of bytes on the surface of a magnetic platter
the property that any location can be reached in the same time as any other
a device whose content is fixed when it is made and can only be read afterwards
items.s: Disk sector: the smallest addressable group of bytes on the surface of a magnetic platter. The other options describe Volatility, Read only memory, Random access.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Seek time.
o: the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed
a fixed sized unit into which a program is divided for movement to and from backing storage
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
the smallest addressable group of bytes on the surface of a magnetic platter
items.s: Seek time: the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information. The other options describe Disk sector, Page, Volatility.

items.q: The correct meaning of Rotational latency is
o: the input that enables one device to answer on the shared lines
the average delay while the wanted sector turns round to the read head
the delay while the head moves to the track that holds the wanted information
the property of losing what is held when the supply is removed
items.s: Rotational latency: the average delay while the wanted sector turns round to the read head. The other options describe Seek time, Volatility, Chip select.

items.q: The correct meaning of Locality of reference is
o: the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon
the arrangement of stores in levels of size and speed, from small and fast to large and slow
the fraction of all requests that are served by the faster level
the fixed sized group of adjacent words moved between two levels
items.s: Locality of reference: the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon. The other options describe Hit ratio, Memory hierarchy, Cache line.

items.q: “a design with a small group of simple fixed length operations that each finish in one cycle” is the definition of
o: Addressing mode
Reduced instruction set
Relative addressing
Operand
items.s: Reduced instruction set is a design with a small group of simple fixed length operations that each finish in one cycle.

items.q: “the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry” is the definition of
o: Decode step
Program counter
Fetch step
Status register
items.s: Status register is the collection of single bits that record whether the last result was zero, negative or produced a carry.
items.t: Processor structure and the instruction cycle

items.q: “the leading bit of a signed word, which shows whether the value is negative” is the definition of
o: Sign bit
Overflow
Floating point notation
Normalised form
items.s: Sign bit is the leading bit of a signed word, which shows whether the value is negative.

items.q: Normalised form may be defined as
o: a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero
the leading bit of a signed word, which shows whether the value is negative
the copying of the leading bit into the new higher places when a short signed word is widened
the constant added to a stored power so that it needs no sign bit
items.s: Normalised form: a floating point arrangement in which the leading digit of the fraction is not zero. The other options describe Exponent bias, Sign bit, Sign extension.

o: Addressing mode
Register transfer notation
Operand
Opcode
items.s: Every other option belongs to Instruction sets and addressing modes. “Register transfer notation” belongs to Register transfer and control, not Instruction sets and addressing modes.

items.q: “a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store” is the definition of
o: Hardwired control
Register transfer notation
Control word
Microprogrammed control
items.s: Microprogrammed control is a scheme in which each step of an instruction is read as a small word from a special store.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Speedup?
o: a clash that arises when a step needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet produced
the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one
the overlapping of successive steps of many instructions in one processor
one of the steps into which the work of an instruction is divided for overlapping
items.s: Speedup: the ratio of the time taken by one arrangement to the time taken by a better one. The other options describe Pipeline stage, Pipelining, Data hazard.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Hit ratio.
o: the tendency of a running program to use the same places and nearby places again soon
a policy in which every change goes to both the faster level and the level below at once
a scheme in which each group from the lower level may go into any of several places above
the fraction of all requests that are served by the faster level

o: Disk sector
Volatility
Rotational latency
Seek time

items.q: “the item of information on which an instruction acts” is the definition of
o: Operand
Immediate value
Indirect addressing
Addressing mode
items.s: Operand is the item of information on which an instruction acts.
